long_biography.plain_text:
Helping establish the Brainerd Lakes Area Economic Development Corporation made Arnold S. Johnson a prominent advocate for creating businesses and jobs in central Minnesota. He also served local banking, college and foundation boards, and helped turn Nisswa lakeshore into public access and parkland through a below-market conservation sale.

That civic influence rested on an entrepreneurial career built with his wife, JoAnn. Johnson founded Universal Pensions in 1975 and developed it from Brainerd into a national retirement-plan services provider for financial institutions. His later interests broadened through Johnson Enterprises and majority stakes in several businesses, while the couple's giving supported education, health and community organisations at home and overseas.
